stem:
Aqueous bromine reacts with methanoic acid to form hydrogen bromide and carbon dioxide gas.

$$\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{HCO}_2\text{H(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{HBr(aq)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

The table shows the oxidation numbers of bromine and carbon in the species involved in this reaction.

|  | Br in $\text{Br}_2$ | C in $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$ | Br in $\text{HBr}$ | C in $\text{CO}_2$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| oxidation number | 0 | +2 | -1 | +4 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify the oxidising agent in this reaction. Explain your reasoning with reference to oxidation numbers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one change you would observe, ignoring temperature changes, when bromine reacts with methanoic acid.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Use the graph to calculate the average rate of reaction at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ during the first 600 s. State the units of this rate of reaction.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The experiment is repeated at a temperature of $40^{\circ}\text{C}$. This relatively small increase in temperature produces a large increase in reaction rate.

Sketch a graph, on the same axes, to show the expected results when repeating the experiment at $40^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The rate of reaction increases when the frequency of successful collisions between reactant particles increases.

Explain why an increase in temperature produces this effect.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Complete the 'dot-and-cross' diagram, showing outer electrons only, to show the bonding in methanoic acid, $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$.
